title: BECE English Studies: Grammar & Structure - English Studies - Parts of Speech - Prepositions
subject: English Studies

questions.q:
Complete the sentence with the correct preposition:
"The manager congratulated him _____ his outstanding performance."
questions.explain: The verb 'congratulate' is idiomatically followed by the preposition 'on'. We congratulate someone 'on' an achievement.
questions.subject: English Studies

questions.q:
Complete the sentence with the correct preposition:
"The CEO is completely averse _____ taking uncalculated risks."
questions.explain: The adjective 'averse' (meaning strongly opposed) is idiomatically followed by the preposition 'to'.
questions.subject: English Studies

questions.q:
Select the appropriate preposition to indicate direction:
"The thief managed to escape by running _____ the dense forest."
questions.explain: 'Through' implies moving directly into one side and out the other side of an enclosed or three-dimensional space, which fits the description of a dense forest better than 'across'.
questions.subject: English Studies

questions.q:
Fill in the correct preposition:
"The suspect was accused _____ stealing the company's funds."
questions.explain: The verb 'accuse' is idiomatically followed by the preposition 'of' when charging someone with a fault or offense.
questions.subject: English Studies

questions.q:
Choose the appropriate preposition to complete the sentence:
"Are you good _____ mathematics?"
questions.explain: In English, to express skill or ability in a subject or activity, we use the phrase 'good at', not 'good in'.
questions.subject: English Studies

questions.q:
Which preposition correctly fills the blank to indicate time?
"The final examination will take place _____ Monday morning."
questions.explain: We use the preposition 'on' for specific days of the week, including phrases that combine the day and the part of the day (e.g., 'on Monday morning').
questions.subject: English Studies
